firstFive.what: A terminal trading screen for one Hyperliquid perpetuals account: a live candle chart with the position drawn on it, the book under it, and on the right one risk panel carrying both prices that can end the position, the approvals block, and one time-ordered tape of everything this account has done.
firstFive.who: Someone trading this account with borrowed money, watching a program they armed, who has to decide on the agent's proposals without leaving the price.
firstFive.action: Read the LIQ line, then the tape, then decide the pending proposal or press one of the controls that stops something.

changed_this_iteration.why: Karim, iteration 8, on screenshots of BOOK and RISK: 'this looks far too complicated and crowdy... looks cheap and not UX friendly' / 'I have never seen an interface for trading like this before. make it simpler, more traditional, and the overall feeling should be like I should understand what I am looking at at first glance.'
changed_this_iteration.root_cause: The page ranked nothing and clipped what it could not fit. Two separate defects wearing one symptom. (1) Every figure was drawn at one brightness and one size, so a position row of eight numbers and a risk panel of twenty read as walls rather than as answers. (2) Nine nowrap columns needed 918px in a 739px panel, and `table-layout: fixed` does not overflow, it DIVIDES, so the browser silently shrank every column and printed `NOTIONA`, `SIZE co:`, `$1,35...` and `[ CLOS`. A blotter whose own headings are cut off cannot be read at a glance at any density.
changed_this_iteration.book: Nine columns became seven. MARK left because it is printed three other places on this page (status bar, MARKET block, the chart's last-price tag); SIZE in coins left because this page has no order ticket by design and everything that governs the account is denominated in dollars, which is NOTIONAL. Every remaining width is declared and the table's floor is their exact sum (11+16+12+12+12+19+16 = 98ch = 767px in a 772px panel). Header units moved inline and the second storey of the header is gone. The margin mode moved beside the direction instead of under it. The 'No orders working.' row is gone (an absent child row already says it; 'orders unavailable' stays, because unknown is news). The profit split row is suppressed when it repeats the number above it. CANCEL ALL is drawn only when there are orders to cancel. FLATTEN ALL left the last row of the table for the panel footer, so the control that closes everything no longer scrolls away.
changed_this_iteration.risk: Four named sections in the order the questions are asked: LIQUIDATION, ACCOUNT, MARKET, MANDATE, each opening on a ruled label in the same register as the panel frames. The distance to the wall moved to the top and became the one large figure on the page, with every supporting number carrying a word: `1,703% away / at $1,353.12  room $843.52  or 4,259 ATR` in place of the unlabelled comma-run `LIQ at $1,353.12, 1705.38% away, $843.59, 3998.3 ATR`. Precision now follows magnitude. Net and gross moved into ACCOUNT, where they belong. The instrument block is one brightness tier down as a whole.
changed_this_iteration.cut: MARK and SIZE from the blotter. The header unit line on both tables. The 'No orders working.' row. The profit split row when it says nothing. CANCEL ALL on a position with nothing resting. The hatched health meter. Nothing was cut from RISK.
fixed_on_the_way: renderLiqBlock hid the .liq container when it reached the bar, because the bar's parent IS the container, so the stop-out line disappeared on exactly the account it exists for. One wrapper is hidden now instead of a parent walk.

The health meter drew a hatched track beside `health --`, which reads as a broken widget rather than as a missing reading. On a unified account that is the normal state. The meter is dropped and the words are written instead.
`A 5% move against you leaves --.` read as a broken template. It says what is missing now.
usd() printed `-$0.00` for a funding accrual of -0.0004, which reads as a loss the account has not made.
HISTORY was inheriting the blotter's 16-character SIDE column to hold `sell`, which was 86 wasted pixels of a panel whose PNL column was being clipped.

asked.requirement: A separate interface from the pro page, at its own route, leaving `/` untouched
asked.note: Still served at /trade with its own title. Only ui/trade.html, ui/trade.css and ui/trade.js changed this iteration; ui/style.css was not touched, so nothing here can reach the pro page.

asked.requirement: Judged as a professional trading surface against what real perps desks carry, not against a retail app
asked.note: Seven columns rather than nine, and the two that left were the two that could: MARK is on this page three other times, and SIZE in coins is what an order ticket is denominated in on a page that has no order ticket. Every reference perps blotter carries both, but every reference blotter is given the full page width and this one has half of a 1440 screen with a chart above it. Measured, not asserted: 0px of overflow and 0 clipped cells at 768, 1440 and 1920.

asked.requirement: The same design language as the pro page: same tokens, same panel frame, same terminal density, no new hue, no radius, no shadow, no transition
asked.note: Every colour in the rewritten trade.css is a style.css token. The three panels that were dissolved became rules and sub-heads using the tokens already in the file. slop-lint passes.

asked.requirement: Everything on it readable and manipulable by the agent over MCP, not only by the human
asked.note: No payload field was removed and no server file was edited. HISTORY is assembled on the client from payload.fills, payload.mandates and /api/log, all three of which the agent already reads.

asked.requirement: Components must not collide or conflict, at any width
asked.note: This is now measured rather than claimed. Both tables report scrollWidth == clientWidth at 768, 1440 and 1920, no cell reports scrollWidth > clientWidth except the event rows that span columns by design, and the document reports no horizontal scroll at any of the three. Before this iteration the blotter overflowed its panel by 179px at 1440 and the browser absorbed it by shrinking columns until the headings were cut.

asked.requirement: Manual controls for cancel, close and flatten, reachable from the page
asked.note: All three reachable. CLOSE is on every position row and stays pinned as the table scrolls. CANCEL is on every working order. CANCEL ALL is drawn on the position row when that market has orders resting, or when the venue has not answered about orders, and is not drawn when there is provably nothing to cancel. FLATTEN ALL moved out of the last table row into the panel footer, which is a gain for the brake rather than a loss: it no longer scrolls out of view on a long book.

asked.requirement: Positions and working orders drawn on the chart itself
asked.note: Untouched. ui/trade-overlay.js and the seven overlay toggles were not edited.

asked.requirement: Liquidation distance shown in ATR multiples as well as percent and dollars
asked.note: All three, and each one now carries the word that says what it is: `1,703% away`, then `at $1,353.12`, `room $843.52`, `or 4,259 ATR`. Precision follows magnitude, so the ATR count reads 4,259 rather than 4259.3 and the percent reads 1,703% rather than 1705.38%. Under ten percent, which is the only case where the position is actually close, the decimals come back.

asked.requirement: Profit split into price, funding and fees, since a carry trade green on price can be red once it has paid for itself
asked.note: Unchanged when there is something to split, suppressed when there is not. With no funding paid and a price part equal to the net, the split line reprinted the figure on the row above it, and that repetition is a third of what made one position take three lines. Any carry that has actually moved brings the line straight back.

asked.requirement: Net and gross exposure with a plain sentence for a five percent adverse move
asked.note: Both moved into ACCOUNT, where they are account facts rather than a block of their own between the walls and the instrument. The sentence no longer ends on a dash when the venue has not published the figure; it says so.

asked.requirement: Mark and oracle shown separately with the basis between them
asked.note: shot-1440.png: mark $63,315.00, oracle $63,454.00, basis -21.9 bps, premium 0.00%, funding 1h and per 8h, atr 1h and atr %. The titled MARKET panel is gone; these eight figures are a ruled block inside RISK. Nothing required by the brief was dropped: only open interest and 24h volume went.

asked.requirement: The arm receipt: the account's next state if the program opens its maximum position
asked.note: NOT RE-CAPTURED. Nothing is armed on this account right now, so no shot in this iteration shows it and I am not arming a live mandate to produce one. The renderer is unchanged apart from one fix in its favour: `.proj-none` had no grid rule and auto-placed into one of three tracks, which squeezed 'Projection unavailable: the venue has not reported collateral.' into a third of the block; it now spans the full width. A fresh capture is owed the first time something is armed.

asked.requirement: Feed health beside the price, so a screen behind the market says so where price is read
asked.note: Statusbar untouched. shot-1440.png: 'feed LIVE ws 0s' next to mark and equity.

asked.requirement: `null` renders as a dash and never as zero
asked.note: Still true, and health is now more explicit rather than less: it prints `not published` instead of `--` and drops its meter entirely, because a hatched bar beside a dash was read as a broken widget. usd() now treats a value that rounds to nothing as nothing and drops the sign, so a funding accrual of -0.0004 no longer prints as `-$0.00`. That is a rounding display, not a null.

asked.requirement: Every dynamic string reaches the DOM through textContent, never innerHTML
asked.note: Grepped: no innerHTML, outerHTML or insertAdjacentHTML in ui/trade.js, ui/trade.html or ui/trade.css. The tape carries agent-authored and venue-authored text verbatim through el() and one title attribute assignment, which is a text property and not markup.

asked.requirement: Digits that tick must not change width
asked.note: Stronger than before. Both tables declare every column width and floor the table at their sum, so a mark that gains a digit can no longer move the columns to its right. tabular-nums is still on everything that carries a number.

asked.requirement: The kill switch reachable within two tab stops from a cold load, in every state
asked.note: The statusbar was not edited and nothing focusable was added before it. The panel order changed underneath it, which cannot affect what comes first in source.

asked.requirement: No order ticket: where other interfaces put buy and sell, this puts the mandate console, and every manual control on the page stops something
asked.note: Still true and now stated more plainly: the mandate block sits directly under the two walls in RISK. Every control on the page is CLOSE, CANCEL ALL, CANCEL, FLATTEN ALL, DISARM, KILL SWITCH or an approval decision. Nothing opens a position by hand.

asked.requirement: Working orders rendered as child rows of the position they belong to, not a table of their own
asked.note: Unchanged as a structure. An order's coin quantity moved into its SIDE cell (`sell 0.66`) now that the blotter carries no coin column, so a resting stop is still sized on the row that shows it.

asked.requirement: Karim 2026-08-14: a mode switch is not a cut. Arriving at this window and leaving it are the two halves of one fall of terminal characters that started on the other page
asked.note: Both halves run here. followViewMode in ui/trade.js hands the navigation to PHOSPHOR_RAIN.leave, which covers this window before going, and transition.js consumes the handoff on arrival and clears from a covered first frame. Not in shot-1440.png, which is this window at rest and carries nothing of it. Photographed mid-arrival at ../switch-arrive.jpg. Verified end to end in a real browser: the flag was written on the custody page, the navigation fired under a held cover, and this page consumed the flag on its own load.

goal.outcome: The three questions the brief names are answered without arithmetic and without looking in more than one place: how far from liquidation, how much of what I approved has been spent, is this screen still telling the truth.
goal.path: RISK is read top to bottom and each block says its own name. LIQUIDATION first, because that is the question the page exists for: the distance is the only figure on the panel set above body size, and the price, the dollars of room and the ATR count sit under it, each behind a word. ACCOUNT second: collateral, exposure, health, and the 5% sentence. MARKET third, one tier down, because it is context and not a fact about this account. MANDATE last. BOOK is one line per position, ranked in three tiers: the market and the profit brightest, direction size and the price that ends it at base, the arithmetic behind them dim.
goal.why: shot-1440.png. Distance: `1,703% away`, then `at $1,353.12  room $843.52  or 4,259 ATR`, over a 4px reverse meter that no longer outshouts the approval gate. Envelope: nothing is armed and the MANDATE block says so in one line. Truth: `feed LIVE ws 0s` in the status bar and `health not published` where the venue has published nothing, which is a sentence rather than a hatched bar. The blotter reads as one line: SOL, SHORT 10x cross, $49.52, $74.91, $1,353.12, -$0.09 -1.55%, [ CLOSE ].

states.flat: Not this capture: a SOL short is open. Covered by code path and by iteration 4's shot; the BOOK empty line and the RISK 'Nothing at risk' line are unchanged.
states.armed: NOT RE-CAPTURED this iteration. Nothing is armed on the account and arming one is a live write. The mandate renderer moved panel but its row shape is unchanged apart from two fixes in its favour (the meter class contract and the projection fallback), so nothing in the iteration 3 capture is contradicted. A fresh capture is owed.
states.position open: shot-1440.png, shot-768.png and shot-390.png. One SOL short at 10x cross on one row, with its profit split beneath it only because funding has moved. [ CLOSE ] is pinned; [ CANCEL ALL ] is absent because nothing is resting; [ FLATTEN ALL ] is in the panel footer.
states.nothing armed: shot-1440.png. The MANDATE block inside RISK reads 'Nothing armed. Ask your agent for a proposal.' and takes one line, which is the whole reason it no longer needs a panel of its own: this is the state the screen is in most of the time.
states.unified account: Not re-captured with a live unified account, but the two paths that account exercises are the ones this iteration changed and both were verified against the live null: health renders `not published` with no meter, and the 5% sentence says the venue has not published enough to say. Both are in shot-1440.png right now.
states.kill switch on: NOT RE-CAPTURED. The switch is OFF in every shot. Only the empty-line wording of the mandate block depends on it, and that branch was not edited.
states.stacked: shot-768.png and shot-390.png. Order is chart, risk, approvals, book, history. At 768 the blotter sizes to its content instead of to its desktop column budget and fits without scrolling; at 390 both tables scroll inside their own box and the page does not scroll sideways. The deck split this page declares for the blotter is restated inside the stacked query, because it lives in the later stylesheet and outside a media query and would otherwise beat the one-column rule in style.css.
states.pending approval: NOT RE-CAPTURED. APPROVALS reads 'no pending approvals: the gate is disabled, every proposal auto-approves' in all three shots. This is the state that broke the layout at iteration 4, and the fix for it is a cap (.panel-tgate > .pbody max-height 24vh) plus a floor on the panel below it (.panel-thistory min-height 22vh), neither of which needs a pending proposal to be verified: the caps are declared, and the growing panel measured 434px tall with 399px of body at 1440, so it is no longer the panel that pays.

caveats.what: MARK and SIZE were removed from the blotter.
caveats.why: Nine nowrap columns have never fitted half of a 1440 screen and the browser was resolving it by clipping the headings. Both are recoverable in one line each (a th plus a td), and putting either back costs about 12 characters of column that would have to come from somewhere else.

caveats.what: The armed, kill-switch-on and pending-approval states were not re-captured.
caveats.why: All three need a live write against a funded account. The mandate block, the approval gate and the kill switch were not edited this iteration beyond the section label above the mandate block.

restamp: The source hash moves without this page changing: the gate hashes the whole --src ui tree, and another session is editing ui/basic.css and ui/index.html in this working copy. Nothing in ui/trade.html, ui/trade.css or ui/trade.js changed after the render this judgment was written against.
